ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Wilma Mankiller — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Six-week review on pyridostigmine and prednisone: strength, breathing, glucose and blood pressure, bone density, start of azathioprine, and the thymectomy plan

text.paragraph: Six-week review on pyridostigmine and prednisone. [S]

Ms. Mankiller returns six weeks after starting prednisone, which reached 40 mg each morning two weeks ago. She had no worsening as the dose rose. Her eyelids droop only late in the evening now, double vision is rare, and she can brush her hair and finish meals without resting. She sleeps less well and feels hungrier, and has gained about 2 kg. She has had no infections. The screening tests drawn at the last visit were normal: TPMT activity normal, hepatitis B surface antigen and core antibody negative with immunity from vaccination, and the tuberculosis blood test negative. She saw the thoracic surgeon two weeks ago, and a robotic thymectomy is planned in five weeks. Her home blood pressure readings average 118/76. She drinks about 2.5 liters of water a day. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1980-05-04; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 128/82 mm Hg; weight 63.9 kg
No ptosis after one minute of upgaze; eye movements full
Neck flexion 5 of 5; arm abduction held for 90 seconds; counts to 50 without a nasal voice

Drooping eyelids and double vision for six weeks, worse in the evening, with fatigable weakness of the arms and neck, tiring when chewing and a nasal voice after long talks; a disorder of the neuromuscular junction suspected
S — Synthetic presenting problem, resolved at the second visit when antibodies and nerve testing established myasthenia gravis.
Generalized myasthenia gravis, acetylcholine receptor antibody positive, MGFA class IIa, without thymoma; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented myasthenia gravis of 1934

S — Synthetic antibody level, electrodiagnosis, class and treatment; the diagnosis less than a year after the crash, and recovery with Cherokee medicine people, surgery and drug therapy, are documented (D).
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (hereditary, as she has described it), with normal kidney function; to be staged
S — The hereditary polycystic kidney disease is documented (D) from her later public account; its detection before the index date, and every value, are synthetic.
Recovery from major trauma in a head-on car crash last year: fractures of both legs, ribs and face, with many operations; walks independently, with a cane on rough ground
S — The crash, the operations and the injuries are documented (D); the current function is synthetic.
Long-term glucocorticoid therapy for myasthenia gravis, with monitoring of glucose, blood pressure, weight, bone health, mood, sleep, eyes and infection
Azathioprine as steroid-sparing therapy, with blood count and liver test monitoring

list.item:
Generalized myasthenia gravis, improving (G70.00). Much improved on prednisone 40 mg and pyridostigmine; MG-ADL 3. Stable enough for thymectomy in five weeks. [S]
Azathioprine 50 mg daily from today, 100 mg daily after two weeks, then 150 mg (about 2.3 mg/kg).
Prednisone stays at 40 mg until after the thymectomy; the taper will start once she has recovered.
Continue pyridostigmine 60 mg four times daily.

Starting azathioprine (Z79.624). TPMT activity normal; the steroid-sparing effect takes several months. [S]
Blood count and liver tests at two, four and six weeks, then every three months.
Report fever, sore throat, unusual bruising, yellow skin or dark urine.

Glucocorticoid therapy (Z79.52). Glucose 104 mg/dL non-fasting; blood pressure 128/82 mm Hg; weight up 2.3 kg; white cells 10.4, as prednisone causes. DXA Z-scores normal (femoral neck -0.4, spine -0.7), so fracture risk is low; calcium and vitamin D continue. [S]
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole three times a week while prednisone is 20 mg or more with azathioprine.
Eye examination within the year.

Next scheduled visit 1980-07-13: review five weeks after thymectomy: recovery, pathology, azathioprine monitoring, the prednisone taper, and kidney care. [S]
